I am farming only a small piece of land here on the slopes of Kilimanjaro, just one-third of a hectare, and I plant beans together with my maize and bananas as we always do. I cannot afford much chemical fertilizer for the beans — beans give their own goodness to the soil — but I will put some manure from my goats and chickens because that is what my mother taught me. I will use the seeds I saved from last season, and I and my daughter will do most of the work ourselves; the rains here are usually enough so I do not need to irrigate.
